# Preface {.unnumbered}

This text provides a self-contained, mathematically rigorous, and fully reproducible presentation of the **Survey-Weighted Dirichlet Process Mixture Model (DPMM)** with **Stratified Cluster Jackknife Variance Estimation** and **Affine Posterior Projection**.

The primary objective is to recover latent subpopulations (phenotypes or disease subtypes) and estimate their finite-population prevalences from complex survey samples—such as stratified, multistage area-probability health surveys—while achieving **calibrated nominal 95% inferential coverage**.

---

## Methodological Overview

Standard Bayesian nonparametric mixture models fit to complex survey data encounter two major challenges:
1. **Selection Bias & Component Fragmentation:** Under unequal-probability sampling, naive likelihood exponentiation ($w_i$-weighting at the individual level) can fragment true clusters and inflate active component counts. The method presented here uses an **unweighted-allocation rule with survey-weighted aggregate updates** under a sparse Dirichlet prior, which automatically empties superfluous components and targets the population mixture.
2. **Cluster Correlation & Uncertainty Calibration:** Complex multistage clustering inflates sampling variability. Standard Bayesian pseudo-posteriors are artificially overconfident. This method employs a **raw-mixture marginal pseudolikelihood Godambe sandwich** where the meat matrix is estimated via a **stratified cluster (delete-PSU) jackknife**, recombined with posterior MCMC mixing uncertainty, and projected via an affine Cholesky transformation to restore nominal coverage.

---

## Mathematical Notation

Throughout this book, we adopt standard survey sampling and Bayesian nonparametric notation:

| Symbol | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\mathcal{U}$ | Finite target population of size $N$. |
| $h = 1, \dots, H$ | Strata in the sampling design. |
| $i = 1, \dots, N_h$ | Primary Sampling Units (PSUs / clusters) in stratum $h$. |
| $j = 1, \dots, M_{hi}$ | Secondary elements (individuals) within PSU $(h, i)$. |
| $n = \sum_{h=1}^H \sum_{i=1}^{n_h} m_{hi}$ | Realized complex sample size ($n \ll N$). |
| $\pi_{hij}$ | Joint inclusion probability $\text{Pr}(j \in \text{sample})$. |
| $w_{hij} = 1 / \pi_{hij}$ | Design weight, normalized such that $\sum_{i=1}^n w_i = n$. |
| $Y_i \in \mathbb{R}^P$ | $P$-dimensional continuous biomarker vector for unit $i$. |
| $z_i \in \{1, \dots, L\}$ | Latent component allocation indicator. |
| $K_0$ | Number of true active population phenotypes ($K_0 < L$). |
| $\pi = (\pi_1, \dots, \pi_{K_0})^\top$ | Population phenotype prevalence vector ($\sum_{k=1}^{K_0} \pi_k = 1$). |
| $H_{\hat\pi}$ | Analytical profile Hessian (bread matrix) of the marginal pseudolikelihood. |
| $J_{\text{jack}}$ | Stratified delete-PSU jackknife covariance (meat matrix). |
| $\Sigma_{\text{sandwich}}$ | Cluster-calibrated sandwich covariance matrix. |
| $\Sigma_{\text{naive}}$ | Empirical MCMC posterior covariance matrix across Gibbs iterations. |
| $\Sigma_{\text{corrected}}$ | Total recombined covariance ($\Sigma_{\text{sandwich}} + \Sigma_{\text{naive}}$). |

---

## Structure of the Book

* **Part I: The Survey-Weighted DPMM** develops the model formulation, the overfitted mixture representation, the unweighted allocation / weighted aggregate update rule, and the C++ Gibbs sampler with zero-waste full-chain draw retention.
* **Part II: Survey-Calibrated Uncertainty Quantification** derives the marginal sub-mixture score equations, the analytical profile Hessian, the stratified cluster jackknife, and the Williams–Savitsky affine Cholesky transformation.
* **Part III: Simulation Benchmark & Implementation** presents the 1,000-replicate Monte Carlo benchmark confirming nominal 95% coverage, along with the complete production R and C++ reference code.
